tasks.title: IconFontFixture: replace the ElementTag regex tag scan with an XDocument walk that still reports an icon-font element carrying '>' inside an attribute value
acceptance: C1.1 (row check, change). `grep -n ElementTag C:/dm-wt/20261123-0703-test-strength-rows/src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/IconFontFixture.cs` prints nothing and exits 1. Must-fire control: at e951be1 the same command prints `56:	private static readonly Regex ElementTag =` and `128:			foreach (Match tag in ElementTag.Matches(text))` (measured by the architect at Gate 2).

C1.2 (row mechanism, cites the backlog row 2026-09-02-app-sub-suite-rebuild 'Migrate IconFontFixture's tag scan from the ElementTag regex ... to an XDocument walk loaded with line info'). The scan parses each XAML text into a System.Xml.Linq.XDocument loaded with LoadOptions.SetLineInfo, selects elements and attributes from the parsed tree, takes each reported line from the element's System.Xml.IXmlLineInfo.LineNumber, and takes Text from the parsed attribute value (already entity-decoded). `grep -n -e "ThemeSource.LineNumber(" -e "ThemeSource.DecodeCharacterEntities(" C:/dm-wt/20261123-0703-test-strength-rows/src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/IconFontFixture.cs` prints nothing; must-fire control: at e951be1 it prints `146:` and `150:` (measured). IconFontAttribute and TextAttribute (e951be1 :61, :66) may stay or be replaced; whichever is used, the recognition rules are preserved: a FontFamily value of `{StaticResource DmFontIcon}` with optional whitespace inside the braces, and an unqualified `Text` attribute (an attribute whose name merely ends in Text, such as `AutomationProperties.HelpText` or a `Label.Text`-style name, is not it, as the e951be1 lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z.])Text` already excludes both). No comment left in the file describes a regex tag scan or comment blanking. Reviewer reads the diff.

C1.3 (seam, change). IconFontFixture exposes one `internal static` method that takes a XAML text and the label to report it under and returns `IReadOnlyList<IconTextDeclaration>`, and the constructor builds `IconTexts` by calling that same method once per file of the real scan (`RepoPaths.AppSourceFiles("*.xaml")`, or `ThemeSource.AppDocuments()`, which enumerates the same files), so the facts in C1.4 exercise the code path the real scan runs and there is no second scan path. Reviewer reads the diff.

C1.4 (new tests, change). A new file `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/IconFontFixtureTests.cs` declares class `IconFontFixtureTests` in namespace `DungeonMaster.Tests.App.Theme` (the namespace the 7 IconFontCoverageTests share, so the C1.5 and C1.7 filters select it) and adds exactly 2 `[Fact]`s and nothing else that runs, each calling the C1.3 method on an inline XAML text, each named for its condition and outcome without claiming more than it asserts (test discipline, Naming, disciplines/test.md:16-18). Fact (a): a MAUI-default-namespace element, starting on a line other than the first, carries an attribute whose value contains a literal `>` (for example `SemanticProperties.Hint="a > b"`) written BEFORE both its `FontFamily="{StaticResource DmFontIcon}"` and its `Text` attribute, with `Text` a numeric character reference such as ``; the fact asserts exactly one declaration whose Where ends `:<that element's start-tag line>`, whose Element is the element name as written, and whose Text is the decoded character. Fact (b), the control that must not fire: the same shape with FontFamily `{StaticResource DmFontBody}` yields no declaration. The `>` must precede both attributes because the e951be1 regex's lazy `[^>]*?` run ends at the first `>`, so an attribute after it is invisible and one before it is not (architect's Python emulation of the e951be1 regex at Gate 2: with the `>` before both attributes the Label's run carried no FontFamily; with the `>` removed it did).

C1.5 (discrimination, disciplines/test.md:35). Show fact (a) can fail by either route: red step (write the facts first against a C1.3 method whose body is still the e951be1 regex logic, IconFontFixture.cs:56-59 and :128-151 at e951be1, applied to the same text), or demonstrated discrimination (with the finished tests, temporarily restore that regex logic as the method body). Under the regex body, run `dotnet test C:/dm-wt/20261123-0703-test-strength-rows/src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~DungeonMaster.Tests.App.Theme.IconFontFixtureTests` (selects exactly the 2 C1.4 facts) and report: fact (a) fails on a FluentAssertions assertion (not an exception), fact (b) passes, summary `Failed: 1, Passed: 1, ... Total: 2`. After the XDocument body is in place, the same command prints `Passed!  - Failed:     0, Passed:     2`. The task report quotes both summary lines, names the method edited and states that the regex body is gone (C1.1 output).

C1.6 (preserved, newly tested). Over the real application tree the scan's population is unchanged. At e951be1 the architect measured 13 declarations two independent ways at Gate 2 (a Python emulation of the e951be1 regex scan over the 27 `.xaml` files outside obj/ and bin/, and a Python XML walk of the same files; both gave 13 and the same entries): Controls/AreaSidebarItem/AreaSidebarItem.xaml:95 Button U+EA8F; :117 Button U+E9FC; Controls/DmDivider/DmDivider.xaml:30 Label U+EAD4; Controls/FloorSidebarItem/FloorSidebarItem.xaml:193 Button U+EA8F; :215 Button U+E9FC; Controls/NotebookView/NotebookView.xaml:78 Label U+EA8F; Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml:96 Label U+EA75; :146 Label U+E97D; :574 Label U+E9FC; :616 Button U+EA8F; Views/DungeonListPage/DungeonListPage.xaml:53 Button U+EA75; :96 Button U+E97D; :123 Button U+E9FC. The implementer dumps `new IconFontFixture().IconTexts` after the change with a throwaway fact or equivalent that is NOT committed (C1.7's count enforces that), and the task report lists the 13 entries it printed and states they equal this list, comparing the path with separators normalised to `/` (e951be1 reported `Path.GetRelativePath` form; either separator is acceptable).

tasks.title: GetDungeonDetailQueryHandlerTests: arrange a non-empty Floors list and assert the handler leaves its elements in place
acceptance: C3.1 (change). `HandleAsync_WithExistingId_ReturnsDtoFromRepository` (GetDungeonDetailQueryHandlerTests.cs:19-39 at e951be1, whose dto passes `[]` for Floors at :24 and asserts `BeSameAs(dto)` at :36) arranges Floors as a mutable `List<FloorDto>` holding at least two distinct FloorDto instances, keeps `result.Should().BeSameAs(dto)` (preserved), and after the call asserts that the list holds exactly those instances, by reference identity, in their original order, with the original count. A `[]` argument cannot exercise in-place mutation: the architect measured at Gate 2 that `[]` for `IReadOnlyList<FloorDto>` arrives as `FloorDto[]`, so a mutating handler throws InvalidCastException instead of mutating. Reviewer reads the diff.

C3.2 (discrimination, remove; row check). Inject into the code under test, `src/DungeonMaster.Application/Features/Dungeons/Queries/GetDungeonDetail/GetDungeonDetailQueryHandler.cs` lines 14-19 (`HandleAsync`, expression-bodied at e951be1): await the repository result into a local, and when it is not null remove the element at index 1 of its Floors in place through a `List<FloorDto>` cast, then return the same instance. The null guard is required so the other two facts, which return null from the repository, keep passing. The architect compiled `var detail = await readRepository.GetDetailAsync(query.Id, cancellationToken); if (detail is not null) { ((List<FloorDto>)detail.Floors).RemoveAt(1); } return detail;` at this site at Gate 2 (block body, one statement per line: 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)). C3.3 (discrimination, replace; row check). Same site and null guard, but replace the element at index 0 in place with a value-equal copy (`detail.Floors[0] with { }`, which record equality calls equal). Run the C3.2 command and report that only the strengthened fact fails, on an assertion (architect's scratch run: `Expected floor to refer to ...FloorDto`; `Failed: 1, Passed: 2`).
